candidates.name: Palace of the Parliament
candidates.price: Adults 60 lei, students 30 lei (19-26 years old, with a valid student ID), children 20 lei (7-18 years old), children under 7 free
candidates.content: The world's second largest building (after the US Pentagon), formerly named "Casa Poporului" (People's House). Building started in 1983 by Nicolae Ceaușescu and is still not completely finished (2019). It spans 12 stories, around

candidates.name: National Art Museum
candidates.alt: Muzeul Național de Artă al României
candidates.price: 24 lei for the Romanian collection, 24 lei for the European collection, or 40 lei for booth; 75% discount for pupils, students (with valid cards), Euro 26 card holders up to 30 years old, and people with disabilities; 50% discount for pensioners
candidates.content: In the building of the former Royal Palace, this museum has collections of ancient, modern and contemporary Romanian art as well as exhibitions of rare European art dating as early as the 14th century

candidates.name: National Museum of Contemporary Art
candidates.hours: Cafe, 4th floor: Open: Tue-Sun 10:00-18; Library (Libraria Jumatatea Plina): Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00; Annex NMCA. Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00. Address: Mosilor 64-68, free entry; Dalles Hall (SALA Dalles) Open: Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00; Address: 18 Avenue N. Balcescu
candidates.content: Inside a converted wing of the Palace of the Parliament, in what had been the private apartments of Ceaușescu, the museum features fresh exhibitions from Romania's burgeoning art scene.

candidates.name: Village Museum
candidates.price: Adult 15 lei; pupils and students (with valid cards) 4 lei; pensioners and Euro 26 card holders 8 lei
candidates.content: An open air museum created in 1934, it now has around 300 traditional buildings (including churches, workshops, mills) and furniture, pottery, clothing gathered from villages in every region of the country in an effort to showcase

candidates.name: Museum of the Romanian Peasant
candidates.content: Also dedicated to the traditional way of life, it focuses mainly on traditional interior decoration, tools, clothing and artifacts. Again, it sometimes hosts folkloric and traditional crafts festivals. ; Small public museum area,

candidates.name: National History Museum
candidates.alt: Muzeul Național de Istorie a României
candidates.content: It's in a neoclassical late 19th-century building, and has exhibits documenting the evolution of society on Romania’s territory from the Paleolithic until today, a replica of Trajan’s Column in Rome and a very interesting collecti

candidates.name: Military History Museum
candidates.content: Has collections of weapons dating since the prehistoric times and permanent exhibitions dedicated to important military events, including the Romanian revolution of 1989, and an outdoor exhibit of relatively modern weaponry, inclu

candidates.name: Museum of Mary and Dr. G. Severeanu
candidates.alt: Muzeul Maria și dr. George Severeanu
candidates.content: The exhibition includes a variety of objects: pieces of archeology - ancient Greek vases, statuettes of Tanagra, bronze and marble, glass Roman items, ancient Greek, Dacian Roman, Byzantine and medieval coins. Romanian and foreign

candidates.name: National Museum of Old Maps and Books
candidates.alt: Muzeul Național al Hărților și Cărții Vechi
candidates.content: Small, but amazing museum with maps on 3 floors. Don’t forget to borrow one of the green magnifying glasses to discover the fine print. Historical maps from 15th-20th century from the whole world with an emphasis on Romania and th

candidates.name: Jewish Community History Museum
candidates.content: Housed in a beautiful mid 19th century synagogue. Documents the life of this community in the region since ancient times and through the Holocaust. Passport required to enter.

candidates.name: Primăveri Palace
candidates.content: The former residence of Ceaușescu, incredibly opulent, one of the most fascinating places to visit in Bucharest. Book online at least a day in advance. Tours last 45 minutes and cover all the main living areas, including the mosai

candidates.name: All Saints' Antim Monastery
candidates.content: An Orthodox monastery in Brâncovenesc style from 1715 with a church, a museum and a shop. The church, museum and shop are open to the public. The church is in the center of a courtyard with the museum and shop in buildings around

candidates.name: Old City
candidates.content: A part of the city's historical heart was not demolished by Nicolae Ceaușescu. The area (stretching approximately between the Dâmbovița river to the south, Calea Victoriei to the west, Calea Moșilor to the east and the Regina Elis

candidates.name: Aviation Museum
candidates.content: Open-air display of various types of aircraft. The museum is closed for renovation from 1 September 2023 and is expected to be closed for 30 months (until 2026).

candidates.name: Curtea Veche Museum
candidates.content: The ruins of the crown palace of the Wallachian princes, some parts dating as early as the 16th century. It’s around an earlier fortification in this place that Bucharest began to develop.

candidates.name: Geology Museum
candidates.content: Has a large collection of minerals, rocks and fossils.

candidates.name: Nicolae Minovici Folk Art Museum
candidates.alt: Muzeul de Artă Populară Prof. Dr. Nicolae Minovici
candidates.content: Also here is Museum of Old Western Art the (Muzeul de Artă Veche Apuseană Minovici). There are collections of the various works of art, such as stained glass from the 16th-17th centuries, engravings, paintings, rare books, tapestr

candidates.name: National Museum of "George Enescu"
candidates.price: Adults 6 lei, seniors 2 lei, students 1.5 lei
candidates.content: Music, memorial museum.

candidates.name: National Philatelic Museum
candidates.content: Come here for stamps, stamp collections, postal items: boxes of values, old paintings, seals, horns, prints, old letters, maps postal coachmen costumes, furniture used in post offices, etc.

candidates.name: Bucharest History Museum
candidates.price: 10 lei and 15 lei extra to take photos (not worth it)
candidates.content: Housed in a palace built in 1834, has collections related to the development of Bucharest from a small 14th-century fortress into Romania’s capital.

candidates.name: Patriarchal Cathedral
candidates.content: Built in 1658. Next to it is the Mitropoliei Palace (1708) – the residence of the Orthodox Patriarch, a sort of small 'Romanian Vatican'. It’s the only church in Bucharest in which photography is prohibited

candidates.name: Plumbuita Monastery
candidates.content: Built in the last half of the 16th century, it once housed the first printing house in the region (1582), today it has a religious objects museum and a large park.

candidates.name: Oțetari Church
candidates.content: The Oțetari Church is a very discreet, spiritual place, giving some religious comfort in the centre of the city. Its name means "cruet", because of the street it is on. It was built in the 18th century and it features a number of

candidates.name: Great Synagogue of Bucharest
candidates.alt: Sinagoga Mare din București, בית הכנסת הגדול של בוקרשט
candidates.content: This decorative temple was raised in 1845 by the Polish-Jewish community. It was repaired in 1865, baroque style, redesigned in 1903 and 1909, repainted in Rococo style in 1936. It hosts an exhibition on the Holocaust in Romanian.

candidates.name: Cotroceni Palace Museum
candidates.content: Has collections of objects that belonged to the former Romanian royal family. Today it is also the residence of the Romanian president.

candidates.name: National Museum of Romanian Literature
candidates.alt: Muzeul Național al Literaturii Române, Casa Krețulescu

candidates.name: D. Minovici Western European Arts Museum
candidates.content: Located in a beautiful eclectic villa

candidates.name: Frederic and Cecilia Cuțescu-Storck Art Museum
candidates.alt: Muzeul de Artă Frederic Storck și Cecilia Cuțescu-Storck
candidates.content: This museum presents works of artists of the Storck family.

candidates.name: Sala Radio
candidates.content: A concert hall that plays an important role in the country's classical music life. Built in 1959 and opened in 1961, it is the country's largest symphonic concert hall.

candidates.name: Cișmigiu Garden
candidates.content: This a lovely small park; it's the oldest in the city (designed 1845-1860). Has boat rental in summer, ice skating in winter time, reasonable restaurants and more specially a French restaurant in Trianon Hotel and several bars.

candidates.name: Herăstrău Park
candidates.content: The largest of several parks around man-made lakes on the Colentina River running through the city’s north and east side) houses the Village Museum, an open-air theater, various sports grounds, an amusement park and numerous resta

candidates.name: Tineretului Park
candidates.content: It has a large multipurpose building (Sala Polivalenta) used for concerts, sporting events, exhibitions, etc., an amusement park for children, boat-rental, several restaurants and bars.

candidates.name: Titan Park
candidates.content: A green oasis among Communist-era high-rise apartment buildings in the eastern part of the city (Titan metro station), has a charming wooden church as well as several lakeside clubs.

candidates.name: Botanical Gardens
candidates.content: Established in 1860, displays a variety of plants from all over the world. The greenhouses are wonderful but have limited opening hours, and are closed Monday, Wednesday and Friday

candidates.name: Filarmonica George Enescu
candidates.content: Housed in the Romanian Atheneum, a city landmark.

candidates.name: Teatrul Național de Operetă Ion Dacian
Carol Park
candidates.content: Designed in 1906, Carol Park has an open-air theater replicating a Roman arena and another construction replicating a medieval fortress. It houses the tomb of the Unknown Soldier as well as an infamous mausoleum built for the Comm

candidates.name: Therme București
candidates.content: Huge thermal water park.

candidates.name: Cinemateca Română
candidates.content: A branch of the National Film Archives, screens mostly classic movies.

candidates.name: Noul cinematograf al regizorului roman
candidates.content: Art films and documentaries selected by major Romanian directors.

candidates.name: Eurocinema
candidates.content: Plays mainly independent European movies.

candidates.name: Cinema Elvira Popescu
candidates.price: 20 lei, carnet of 5 tickets: 70 lei, children under 12: 10 lei
candidates.content: Mostly French movies.

candidates.name: Cinema City
candidates.content: Largest multiplex in the city (21 screens, including one IMAX).

candidates.name: Hollywood Multiplex
candidates.content: This was the first multiplex to open in Bucharest and has 10 screens.

candidates.name: Movieplex
candidates.content: Located in the western part of Bucharest, has 11 screens.

candidates.name: Europa
candidates.content: Plays relatively recent European movies.

candidates.name: Queen’s Club
candidates.price: Entry 20 lei, but that includes 10 lei worth of drinks at the bar
candidates.content: Like gay clubs the world over, this place has become tremendously popular with a hetero set fed up with the meat market atmosphere at so many of the city’s other locations. That, together with superb music, makes this an essential

candidates.name: Interbelic
candidates.content: Cocktail bar; fine spirits, great nights.

candidates.name: Club A
candidates.content: The oldest club in Bucharest, with nearly 40 years tradition (this means amazingly much for a city where most clubs are less than 5 years old). Since the beginning, it was and remains a student pub and club, with an unpretentious

candidates.name: Expirat/OtherSide
candidates.content: Very lively and popular club, divided in two sections - Expirat, the old club with rock/dance/hiphop music, and its newer offspring, the OtherSide, where DJs spin electronica. Themed nights, very expat-friendly, great cocktails an

candidates.name: Kulturhaus
candidates.content: A club with a German concept – ”the culture house” – a place where all sort of cultural events (such as live music concerts, art exhibitions, film projections) take place. Kulturhaus is very cheap – no entry fee (except for music

candidates.name: Absintherie Sixtină
candidates.content: Classic style bar with reasonable prices. The absinthe is served with a slow drip fountain.

candidates.name: Beer O'Clock
candidates.content: Bar with several types of Belgian, Czech and Slovak beer.

candidates.name: Curtea berarilor
candidates.content: Pub in old center having mostly Timișoreana beer.

candidates.name: Green Hours
candidates.content: A quiet club which often hosts jazz concerts.

candidates.name: BEAT bar umanist
candidates.content: Nice cosy bar near Unirii/old town.

candidates.name: Bamboo
candidates.content: It's the largest club in Bucharest. Upmarket and expensive.

candidates.name: Cafe Hazard
candidates.content: A rock bar, with a great atmosphere, open thinking, great beer and people.

candidates.name: Restaurant Hanu' lui Manuc
candidates.content: Great location in Bucharest city centre and wonderful traditional food.

candidates.name: Caru' cu Bere
candidates.content: One of the most famous restaurants in Bucharest, in a historic building.

candidates.name: LUCA
candidates.content: Cheap Romanian traditional pastry chain with locations all over the city (and much of Romania, and even Poland). There are both sweet and savory products. Good for vegetarians. Huge selection of pastries for all tastes. Most popul

candidates.name: Locanta Jaristea
candidates.content: Beautiful historically themed restaurant, live traditional music, old Romanian specialties; but always check the bill thoroughly. Reservations are compulsory.

candidates.name: Casa di David
candidates.content: Opened in 2005, it is a hangout of the city's nouveau riche. It comes complete with German car ads at the entrance and an extensive wine list. Food (Italian inspired) and ambience are OK, but portions are small and prices are far

candidates.name: Kanteen 162
candidates.content: Very good food, consistent menus, impeccable service and kind staff. Best place to find the traditional taste of organic food.

candidates.name: Bodega "La Mahala"
candidates.content: A secluded and quiet place hidden a bit among the noisy and losing western-style pubs of the Old Town. It has an intimate and a bit old-fashioned Romanian look which gives it the feeling of the 90s with some more modern elements.

candidates.name: Cuptorul cu lemne
candidates.content: A nice pizza place with a nice outdoor summer garden and a relaxed atmosphere (the restaurant also houses a caricature club). Tends to be very crowded during weekends.

candidates.name: Rossetya 2.0
candidates.content: Classic style restaurant with prices a bit higher than average, but with a very neat and cultivated atmosphere, outstandingly friendly English-speaking personnel, high food quality.

candidates.name: Taj Indian Cuisine
candidates.content: Good Indian restaurant near Marriott hotel, especially for vegetarians.

candidates.name: Il Bocconcino - Restaurant si livrare Popesti-Leordeni
candidates.content: Italian restaurant.

candidates.name: Red Angus Steakhouse
candidates.content: In the Old Center, across the street from the Old Court. The restaurant serves high quality USDA Choice beef and offers an excellent, diverse menu, for all tastes. Also at 56 Franceza St.

candidates.name: Jolie Ville Galleria
candidates.content: Mega Image hypermarket, services: Florists, pharmacies, cleaners.

december.text: Bucharest, like most of Romania, has a temperate-continental climate with hot summers and cold winters. This region of Romania gets all four seasons, although spring is brief and falls mainly in April. The average high daily temperature in summer is about 29 °C and in winter about 2 °C.
